page: Microsoft Azure E20a_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine hosted via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.35 GHz across 10 physical cores and 20 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent. Memory provisioning is robust with 160.0 GB of RAM, equating to an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A 537 GB local SSD is included, whereas no dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

In synthetic and system benchmarks, the memory subsystem demonstrates high capability, marked by a PassMark memory score of 2786.72 and large-block uncached read bandwidth of 78.56 GB/sec alongside cached read speeds reaching 1293.37 GB/sec. Multi-threaded compute throughput sits in the average tier, logging a Geekbench multi-core score of 11374.0, a PassMark CPU score of 24051.11, and 7695.53 on stress-ng. Conversely, single-thread processing displays lower relative efficiency, with single-core stress-ng indexing in the lower percentiles. In-memory data throughput achieves 20.38 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and static web serving hits 17.36 GB/sec.

Architectural tradeoffs center around memory density versus raw compute and vector acceleration. Without AVX-512 or dedicated GPU accelerators, medium-scale model inference struggles, showing weak text generation speeds. However, the generous 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation coupled with integrated local SSD storage provides high cost efficiency for memory-centric operations compared to overprovisioning high-compute instances. Microsoft Azure E20a_v4 is targeted for memory-intensive workloads, including distributed in-memory key-value databases, enterprise relational databases, ETL data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E20a_v4 is a memory-optimized instance providing 20 dedicated vCPUs backed by 10 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.35 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance integrates 160 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes 537 GB of local SSD storage without dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong memory subsystem performance, reaching a PassMark memory score of 2786.72 and uncached read bandwidth of 78.56 GB/sec. General multi-core processing registers mid-tier results with a PassMark CPU score of 24051.11, while single-core compute performance exhibits lower relative throughput. The absence of AVX-512 and hardware accelerators makes it less optimal for intensive AI generation, but the high memory density provides cost-effective efficiency for memory-bound applications. The E20a_v4 is well suited for in-memory caching solutions like Redis, relational database management systems, and large-scale data aggregation.
